topIssues.title: Improve context + clean up context slop
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Optimize the context sent to the model so action/tool search works efficiently and the agent gets only what it needs to complete the task.

## Detailed Description

**Estimate:** 5 working days. **After:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/31014

Use the existing context editor and trajectory viewer.

- Review representative runs to identify unnecessary instructions, duplicate context, irrelevant provider output and oversized tool descriptions/results.
- Improve context selection and composition: include what the current task needs and retrieve additional context when needed. Remove redundancy at its source rather than silently cutting off payloads.
- Verify action/tool search finds the right capabilities with concise queries, useful rankings and minimal repeated searches. Fix missed tools, irrelevant matches and unnecessary tool loading.
- Use the existing edit, rerun and compare loop to measure input tokens, retrieval overhead, latency, tool choices and task success. Record the context changes and model/settings used.
- Check both simple and multi-step tasks. Reduce context without losing required facts, tool arguments or reliable task completion.

- Correct Cloud usage attribution before comparing runs: map native `promptTokens`/`completionTokens` to the usage-event `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` contract in buffered, SSE and non-SSE fallback paths. Check current behavior and reuse applicable #27744 work.
- Verify emitted input/output/total counts match gateway usage, including a final SSE usage-only frame. Verify downstream cost estimates use the real counts when gateway cost is absent; retain unknown usage as unavailable. This fixes telemetry, not server-side credit debits.

Cloud token counts #27732 is consolidated here within the same five-day allocation. Original reproduction and consumer details remain linked in that issue.

**Done when:** before/after trajectories show lower unnecessary context and efficient action/tool search, with the agreed tasks still completing correctly. Record token and latency changes, failures and any tradeoffs. Missing usage stays unknown; estimates are labeled.

Reruns, comparison, validation and targeted fixes are included in the five days. This ticket does not build another context editor.

[Project and schedule](https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/20)

topIssues.title: fix(app): expose actionable local backup size-limit failures
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
The running macOS app cannot create a backup of the current agent state, and the dialog hides the deterministic size rejection behind “Backup failed.” Retrying the same state cannot succeed.

Reproduced in signed development bundle a0de6f6cc43e8c086f12a2fbf1b932b91a7bee63: Settings → Backups → Back up agent → Create Backup. The dialog remains open with an error; no backup was created and no restore was attempted. Sanitized runtime diagnostic at 2026-09-06T19:11:54.645Z: `Snapshot refused during file capture: source budget exceeded`.

`POST /api/backups` calls `createLocalAgentBackup`, which uses the v1 snapshot path. `AgentSnapshotBudgetExceededError` already carries code, stage, observed bytes and limit bytes. The route catches every failure and sends generic HTTP 500. The v1 shared restore ceiling is 128 MiB; source capture also accounts for allocation overhead. Do not raise that cap, truncate content, or omit state to make this test pass.

Acceptance:

- Translate the known typed budget rejection to a structured, safe response without filesystem paths or database diagnostics.
- Show an actionable size-limit explanation in the native backup dialog and distinguish it from a retryable transport/storage failure.
- Exercise the real route/error boundary and UI consumer, including an ordinary unexpected failure; preserve full backup data and existing limits.
- Confirm whether the supported large-state local backup path is the existing v2 streaming implementation. Keep full backup success explicitly unverified until a created artifact is inspected and a restore is verified in isolated state.
- Capture the native result in the rebuilt revision; the current observation is a failure, not acceptance proof.

topIssues.title: Reconcile Cloud pricing, credit provenance, retention, and payment policy
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## Parent / scope

Follow-up to #22942. Make every advertised container charge either enforced with a receipt or removed from the product contract.

## Problem

Container constants advertise deploy, image, monthly reference, storage, bandwidth, and extra-instance charges, but the audited production callers only establish daily CPU/memory/count billing. These are ghost prices until code and ledgers prove otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory every container rate constant and its authoritative caller/ledger/receipt.
- [ ] Obtain product approval for exact prices and units; do not infer missing rates.
- [ ] Remove unused rates and UI/docs promises, or implement idempotent metering and settlement with exact numeric tests.
- [ ] Expose only actually active charges through the canonical snapshot and active-billing API.
- [ ] Prove replay, partial failure, and concurrent billing behavior for each retained charge.

## Non-scope / overlap fence

Do not modify #22553's selected/deleting/failed billable semantics or #22906's container-delete reconciliation.

topIssues.title: Packaged macOS startup presents ready UI before embedded first-run completes
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
A clean single-instance launch of the current macOS development package exposes chat and Settings while its embedded backend is still an unconfigured first-run server.

Observed on the real Mac with the packaged renderer (build content ID 15a2d61edd19, source 4582587bee3):
- Embedded API correctly moves to port 31338 because 31337 is occupied.
- Backend logs: fresh install; runtime boot deferred until onboarding commits.
- Direct read-only API checks: auth/status required=false, authenticated=false; first-run/status complete=false; status state=not_started; runtime/mode mode=local.
- Renderer nevertheless logs remote-backend, skips local startup, and reaches ready.
- Desktop bootstrap returns 503 db_unavailable. Native chat fails to send.
- Cloud sign-in remains on Opening Cloud sign-in without opening Safari; the same result reproduced after eliminating an initial duplicate-app launch.

The exact mechanism linking the stale/restored client target, first-run classification, and the stuck sign-in is still being investigated. Do not treat the backend first-run state as successful setup or bypass authentication to make the controls appear usable.

Acceptance: on the packaged app, an unconfigured embedded backend leads to a usable setup path; Cloud sign-in opens and completes or shows a bounded actionable failure; setup initializes the real backend and a native chat reply succeeds. Retest returning configured profiles and occupied-port startup without discarding their setup.

topIssues.title: x402 pooled settlement via Concord channels
topIssues.author: gazoy
topIssues.body:
Following #32576, which adds x402 payments to Eliza: Concord keeps the x402 request and response headers (X-PAYMENT, X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE, the 402 `accepts` body) but lets an agent pay through a payment channel or a shared pool, so a session of calls settles in one on-chain transaction and the agent's spend is capped by a policy enforced on its account rather than in plugin code.

Reference implementation, tests and demo: https://github.com/gazoy/concord (Python; Cosmos SDK port planned). The demo runs an agent paying an API per call and the API settling once.

I'd like to build an Eliza plugin for it (a payment scheme alongside the existing x402 one) and am looking for a maintainer to sanity-check the design. Happy to open a draft PR if there's interest.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud,agent): finish manifest-v3 restore coordinator and wire the restore route
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Re-lands manifest-v3 restore and finishes the restore coordinator, so a user restore of a catalogued manifest-v3 backup now runs end to end in production code: quarantined create → materialize → commit → boot → attest → probe → route CAS → finalize. Refs #20726 ## #20732: restore coordinator Fixes #20732. Everything is in code and tested against real PGlite. The only thing left is the staging drill listed below. ### Re-land (commit 1) - Cherry-picks `9ab8150880c`, which ports closed #30820 and standujar's `feat/20732-quarantine-runtime-bridge` onto current `develop`. standujar keeps `Co-authored-by` credit. - It applied cleanly on top of #32876, the #31334 local-state upgrade guard; the two touch different files. - `packages/agent/FOOTPRINT-REVIEW.md` now records that the owner reversed the removal of the restore-v3 candidate modules for #20732. ### Phases The existing phase names map onto the requested ones: - `restoring` means materialized. - `committed` means the generation is committed. - `restart_attested` means booted and attested. - `probed` means probes passed. - `published` means routed. | From → to | What the coordinator does | | --- | --- | | `reserved`/`vault_seeded` → `container_created` | Runs the existing exact quarantined create. An ambiguous provider outcome goes through the existing claim-fenced reconciliation. | | `container_created` → `restoring` | 1. Starts the quarantine host.
2. Prepares private roots inside the container (new controller worker). Their device/inode identities are recorded.
3. Streams the catalogue into the quarantine through the guarded materializer journal, using the worker's KMS key bundle and the storage registry. Each object uses its own persisted endpoint.
4. Records the sealed candidate receipt and session. | | `restoring` → `committed` | Prepares and commits the generation inside the still-networkless container, then records the committed-generation handoff. | | `committed` → `restart_attested` | 1. Snapshots the previous route and observes the previous runtime.
2. Stops the previous runtime **in place** (it is retained, so it can be restarted).
3. Serving transition: detaches the exact container from `none`, attaches the agent network (which activates host ports reserved at create) and restarts the quarantine PID 1.
4. Hands over a boot grant.
5. Launches the committed generation.
6. Polls a private-socket probe until it returns an HMAC-signed boot attestation under the per-restore activation token.
7. Sandbox activation moves `restore_pending` → `restart_attested` and the operation advances, in one transaction. | | `restart_attested` → `probed` | Runs three fresh-nonce signed probes. Each checks the MAC, the identities, the committed-generation digest and the listen port. | | `probed` → `published` | Route CAS, in one transaction:
- proves the canonical route still equals the snapshot;
- adopts the provider-settled replacement (`lifecycle_committed`);
- activates the generation (`active`, published/dispatched/completed);
- points `sandbox_id`/`node_id`/`container_name`/`bridge_url`/`health_url`/`image_digest` at the restored container. | | `published` → `finalized` | 1. Appends the immutable activation publication from the active generation.
2. Removes the previous container, bound to its identity, and releases its node slot once.
3. Writes the final restore receipt (`commitAgentBackupRestore`, backup → `restore_verified`).
4. Finalizes the operation with the receipt and releases the lease. | ### Failure policy (fail closed at each phase) - **Before the previous runtime is touched:** failures retry with exponential backoff up to `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. After that the restore activation is blocked and the operation fails terminally. The route never moves. - **After the previous runtime is stopped** (`committed`, `restart_attested`, `probed`): any failure rolls back. The restored container is stopped, the retained previous runtime is restarted, the activation is blocked, the operation fails terminally and the lease is released. If rollback is incomplete, the operation is recorded as `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_ROLLBACK_INCOMPLETE` and the error is rethrown so an operator is alerted. - **Cleanup after a terminal failure:** the failed container is fenced (`cleanup_in_progress`) before it is removed exactly. It is then settled as `cleanup_proven`, and its node slot is released once. Settling frees the agent's replacement fence, so later restores and upgrades are not blocked. A cycle sweep retries any interrupted cleanup. A later restore may replace the `blocked` activation that the failed restore left behind. - **After the route CAS:** rollback no longer applies. Finalization retries until it settles. - **Lapsed lease:** an operation whose lease lapsed with no live claim is closed explicitly as `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_LEASE_EXPIRED`. - **Evidence is write-once:** every piece of phase evidence lives in `agent_backup_restore_operations.serving_state` (migration `0495`, journal updated). A lost response therefore replays and never re-executes. ### Production caller - `POST /api/v1/eliza/agents/:agentId/restore` → `elizaSandboxService.restore()` → `admitCoordinatedAgentBackupRestore`. - When `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_COORDINATOR_ENABLED=1` and the selected backup is a catalogued manifest-v3 backup in a restorable state, the route acquires the restore lease for `AGENT_BACKUP_RESTORE_WORKER_ID`, opens the operation and returns **202** with the operation id. - A second request reports the in-progress restore. Another coordinator's restore returns 409. - Legacy snapshot rows keep the existing push/re-provision path. - The coordinator runs as a `restore-coordinator` stage of the existing backup-catalogue worker daemon. That stage shares the worker's KMS key bundle and storage registry. ### Deliberate change to the quarantine create - Docker cannot add port bindings to an existing container. The exact quarantine is therefore created with its two host ports reserved (`-p`), still attached only to `none`, where the bindings are inert. - The create readback and every command fingerprint now require the reserved bindings. - The only transition that attaches a network is the coordinator's serving transition, after the committed generation is proven. ### Agent side - `agent-backup-restore-v3-controller-worker`: one-shot, private, with three methods: `prepareRoots`, `commitGeneration` and `writeBootGrant`. - `agent-backup-restore-v3-restored-runtime`: boots `startEliza({ restoredGeneration })` behind an exclusive lock and serves signed attestations on a 0600 unix socket. - `agent-backup-restore-v3-probe-client`: relays one probe. - Contract: `@elizaos/core/contracts/agent-backup-restore-v3-serving`. - Agent restore tests had wall-clock test budgets that timed out under load. Those budgets are now load-tolerant. Assertions and deliberately short expiry deadlines are unchanged. ### Remaining: staging drill (needs an authorized staging run) 1. On a real Hetzner node, confirm Docker accepts `-p` with `--network none` at create. Then confirm that `docker network disconnect none` followed by `docker network connect ` on the stopped exact container activates the reserved bindings. 2. Confirm the built image ships the three new `dist/services/*.js` entrypoints and the new core contract in `packages/core/dist`. Confirm the runtime launched with `docker exec -d` (using the image's `/opt/tsx` loader) inherits the agent env and binds `ELIZA_PORT`. 3. Restore a real agent and verify functional LLM recall of pre-backup memory through the published `bridge_url`. 4. Exercise a forced probe failure and confirm the previous runtime restarts. ## #24407: fair admission and legacy cron Refs #24407. Verified; the cron is **not** retired. - The minute admission (`/api/v1/cron/agent-backup-admission`) is fair: 64 sharded durable cursors, bounded per-invocation claim and enrollment budgets, and explicit deferral. - It only enrolls agents whose activation is `active` with published activation authority. Before this PR nothing in production wrote that state. After it, only coordinator restores do. - Retiring the six-hour `enqueueScheduledBackups` caller would therefore leave every legacy agent with no scheduled backup. - The cron comment now records this. Retirement needs an activation backfill for legacy agents first; the admission route stays gated off (`AGENT_BACKUP_ADMISSION_CALLER_ENABLED=0`). ## #23235: capture escalation and stranded-row plan Refs #23235. - A capture operation that keeps failing retryably is escalated once it reaches `AGENT_BACKUP_CAPTURE_ESCALATION_ATTEMPTS` claims (default 8). The typical case is the available-memory gate. - The escalated failure becomes a trusted **terminal** disposition, `AGENT_BACKUP_V2_CAPTURE_ESCALATED`. It carries the exact spool-cleanup authority, so it settles through the vetted terminal path. - The worker raises `BACKUP_CAPTURE_V2_ESCALATED` and logs the org and backup. - Stale-runtime-authority failures are never escalated. ### Plan for repairing stranded rows (not executed; live customer rows) 1. **Inventory (read-only).** Collect every `agent_sandboxes` row in `deletion_pending`/`deletion_failed` older than 24h. For each, record its last error, `deletion_attempt_id`, `bridge_url`, node and whether a container is present (observe only). 2. **Classify.** - (a) node-unreachable, where the node is now reachable; - (b) permanently failed on a since-fixed defect (#23117 `toISOString`, job timeout); - (c) capture refused, where the customer wants the state gone; - (d) the container is already absent. 3. **Repair per class, through existing lifecycle authority only (no raw SQL).** - (a)/(b): re-enqueue deletion with `reEnqueueFailedDeletions`. - (d): run the reap path, which releases the allocation. - (c): run `shutdown` with `stateLossAcknowledged` under an operator-recorded authorization. 4. **`bridge_url` after reap.** Clear it in `releaseDeletionAllocationOnReap`, so a later attempt does not refuse on a dead bridge. This is a small follow-up code change with a PGlite regression test. 5. **Dry run, then execute.** Dry-run in staging, then run in production with an operator present. Take a before/after row diff as the audit record. Still open under #23235: the customer-reachable acknowledged-state-loss delete path. ## Verification - `bun test src/lib/services/__tests__/agent-backup-restore-coordinator.pglite.test.ts` (cloud-shared): 4 pass. Covers full finalize, forged-probe rollback, pre-boot retry/resume and target selection. - `bun test src/lib/services/agent-backup-capture-v2-escalation.test.ts`: 4 pass. - Existing restore/worker suites: - `agent-backup-restore-coordinator-runtime.test.ts`: 3 pass. - `agent-backup-restore-operations-migration.test.ts`: 7 pass. - `agent-backup-restore-v3-materialization.pglite.test.ts`: 1 pass. - `backup-catalog-worker.pglite.test.ts`: 1 pass. - `account-deletion-backup-authority-cycle.pglite.test.ts`: 1 pass. - `tsc --noEmit` passes for cloud-shared and cloud-api. `check:router-contract` and `check:worker-bundle` pass for cloud-api. - Biome is clean on the changed files. - Agent (vitest, one file at a time): - new `agent-backup-restore-v3-controller-worker.test.ts`: 3 pass - new `agent-backup-restore-v3-restored-runtime.test.ts`: 2 pass - `agent-backup-restore-v3-candidate-assembly.test.ts`: 10 pass - `agent-backup-restore-v3-generation-commit.test.ts`: 3 pass - `agent-backup-restore-v3-materializer-process.test.ts`: 9 pass - `agent-backup-restore-v3-pglite-archive.test.ts`: 37 pass. Its gzip-dump case had failed on its old 90s budget; it now takes 133s. - `runtime/restore-generation.boot.test.ts`: 2 of 4 pass (unfinished-generation, server-restart). - "initializes and restarts the real runtime…" hangs well past its per-test timeout: more than 30 min, with no timeout ever reported. - The re-land commit's unmodified version of this file hangs on the same case on this machine, past its original 120s budget. So the hang already exists in the re-land and is not a budget problem. It looks like a blocked event loop during real runtime initialization under load. - Needs an unloaded run or CI to confirm. - The Docker suites are opt-in (`AGENT_RESTORE_V3_DOCKER_TESTS=1`) and were not run. - `tsc --noEmit` passes for agent and core. - Not run: `bun run verify`. The machine was heavily loaded, with a load average of 25–37. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: Reduce planner context overhead and preserve task completion through scoped discovery
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Action tasks loaded unrelated schemas, sometimes finished without requested readback, and rebuilt avoidable prompt context. Simple arithmetic could unnecessarily enter evaluation. Paused work could lose its original domain when the response handler returned a simple reply.

# Change

Keep the response handler focused on contexts and intents. Use task-scoped `DISCOVER_ACTIONS`, operation-specific schemas, canonical tool ordering, stable evaluator instructions and instruction-aware cache affinity. Document verification/reference codes no longer infer programming work. Complete authorized source text and receipts remain intact.

Continue against every requested outcome, with prerequisite barriers, verified receipts, explicit additional-budget resume, fresh authorization and cancellation. Saved schemas are not reused. Ambiguous effects are parked rather than replayed. Preserve external continuation-worker fixes. Completed simple answers stay on the one-call path.

Preserve exact FILE bytes and final-line-ending evidence. A scoped native object envelope addresses observed Cerebras Qwen argument boundary loss while retaining native schemas, validation, cancellation and canonical hooks. Other providers and handler/evaluator transport are unchanged. Distinguish document identifiers from integrity metadata in evaluation.

# Testing

Current candidate: `ce005a06184a4e8c643bc92b33614259a7a02c77`; integrates develop through `93406451`.

- Owning integration qualification: **465 tests passed** across evaluator (85), discovery (82), Cloud usage (123), navigation (59), and contextual retrieval (116).
- Final follow-up: **71 routing tests**, **59 navigation tests**, full assistant and agent typechecks, and scoped Biome passed. Exact file I/O with empty model contexts no longer adds coding-task hints; explicit coding, delegation and mixed source refactoring remain preserved.
- Both preserved eight-task cohorts at `6de0cc10`: **8/8 passed each**, with exact bytes, readbacks and requested replies. First: 29 foreground calls, 131,984 input / 63,488 cached / 68,496 fresh (48.10%). Warm repeat: 31 calls, 150,765 input / 90,112 cached / 60,653 fresh (59.77%). All 12 continuation comparisons retained complete evidence and stable system/tool/schema prefixes. These are separate unpaired observations, not a causal speedup or universal cache target.
- Text and synthetic PCM STT→agent→TTS at `6de0cc10` passed with one handler call and one user/assistant pair each; 2,455 input / 2,048 cached (83.4%). Physical microphone/speaker acceptance is not claimed.
- Fresh final-head HTML and two-file acceptance: **2/2 passed** with exact bytes, readbacks and replies. Eight foreground calls reported 40,634 input / 22,528 cached / 18,106 fresh (55.44%); both continuation comparisons preserved complete prefixes. All three planner calls used the same five tools and 7,691 schema bytes. Live handlers chose files directly; the empty-context repair is verified by regression tests.
- Fresh final-head text and synthetic PCM voice: **passed**; one handler call and one user/assistant pair each, 2,455 input / 2,048 cached (83.4%).
- Hosted exact-head checks: **all passed**. Clean-head `bun run verify`: **passed**, 284/284 package tasks; final audits scanned 7,082 test files with no focused tests or orphaned skips. Source remained clean and unchanged throughout. The earlier `6de0cc10` failure and superseded root run remain recorded; neither is labeled a pass.

Deterministic registered messaging schemas shrink from 23,627 to 10,487 bytes for generic messaging, and 13,973 to 2,274 bytes for inbox search. Full schemas and authorized catalog discovery remain available. Five effect-free live probes selected suitable calls; connector effects were not executed.

The preserved historical study has all 30 pairs and failures. On 15 common successful pairs with complete usage, calls fell 92→56 and fresh input 296,288→114,140 (61.5% less); weighted cache share was 57.8%→58.8%. Historical acceptance is confounded by provider/client/admission failures and is not final-head reliability evidence.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud-billing): retire creator payouts, disclose affiliate surcharge, add funding-stop retention
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
These are owner-decided Cloud billing policies: subscription (Plus/Pro) plus pay-as-you-go, with mini-app capabilities already removed. The tracker is #22957 and the policy table is in merged #32864. Migrations are **0500**, **0501** and **0502**; 0496–0499 are left for another branch, and the journal is updated.

Refs #22957

## #22961 / #23022: creator monetization retired (affiliates stay live)

Fixes #22961
Fixes #23022

**Accrual stopped. History kept.**
- MCP calls (`recordUsage`, `recordUsageWithoutDeduction`) no longer write either creator leg: no creator org credit and no `mcp` redeemable earning. New `mcp_usage` rows record `creator_earnings = 0`. The base price and platform fee go to `platform_earnings`, and the buyer charge is unchanged.
- Agent inference markup and app creator monetization are switched off by 0500. Turning either back on returns HTTP 410 with `code: creator_monetization_retired`; this is a typed `CreatorMonetizationRetiredError` that extends `ApiError`.
- Earnings-funded hosting (`pay_as_you_go_from_earnings`) was an automatic payout of the frozen balance. 0500 turns it off and sets the column default to false. The settings API refuses to turn it back on, and an account-deletion restore no longer re-enables it.
- No ledger rows are deleted or rewritten.

**Creator payout entry points.** Each of these now returns a typed 410:
- `POST /api/v1/redemptions` and `GET /api/v1/redemptions/quote`
- admin approve in `POST /api/admin/redemptions` (admin reject still works; it returns the pending lock to the frozen balance)
- `POST /api/v1/apps/:id/earnings/withdraw`
- `POST /api/cron/process-redemptions`, which is also removed from the cron schedule

The on-chain payout processor and the `lockForRedemption` / `refundRedemption` / `convertToCredits` helpers are deleted. Redemption history and the balance read (now always `canRedeem: false`) stay.

**Affiliate payouts stay live.** The affiliate program continues; only creator, MCP and app monetization is retired.
- `POST /api/v1/earnings/payout/stripe-connect/onboard` is restored for users who have an affiliate code. Anyone else gets 403.
- `POST /api/v1/earnings/payout/stripe-connect/transfer` is restored. It is still admin-gated and still a compensating saga. It now debits through `affiliate-payouts.ts`, and a definitive Stripe rejection re-credits the amount as an affiliate earning. No cron is needed, because an operator triggers each transfer.
- **The gate.** A payout may debit at most `min(affiliate net since retirement, available balance − frozen available)`. "Affiliate net since retirement" is the sum of the user's `affiliate` ledger earnings and adjustments after the retirement instant: the user's statement `frozen_at`, or the new `creator_monetization_retirement.retired_at` singleton written by 0500.
  - The check and the debit run in one transaction under the same per-user advisory lock as the ledger, so concurrent payouts cannot both pass.
  - A same-key retry reuses the prior debit.
  - Anything more returns 409 `affiliate_payout_exceeds_payable`.
  - Non-affiliate earnings after retirement (revenue shares and similar) are not payable through this path.
- **Not payable here:** affiliate earnings that were already unpaid at retirement. They are inside the frozen statement and are settled manually with it.
- The statement shows `affiliatePayableUsd`, and the Earnings tab shows it as "Affiliate earnings available for payout".

**Freeze and statement.**
- 0500 copies every user's unpaid balance (`available_balance + total_pending`) into `creator_earnings_retirement_statements`, broken down by source. The table has no foreign keys, so the record survives account deletion. The copy is idempotent.
- `GET /api/v1/earnings/statement` returns the read-only statement.
- The Monetization "Earnings" tab now shows this statement. The redemption UI, the app earnings dashboard, the withdraw dialog and the app monetization settings are removed.

### Follow-up for manual handling: affected orgs and amounts

No local database was reachable (`DATABASE_URL` unset, nothing on localhost:5432), so this lists no orgs or amounts; it gives the queries to run instead. Run them against production **after 0500 is applied**:

```sql
-- Frozen creator balances per organization (what is owed)
SELECT s.organization_id, o.name AS organization_name,
       count(*) AS users, sum(s.unpaid_balance_usd) AS unpaid_usd,
       sum(s.available_balance_usd) AS available_usd,
       sum(s.pending_redemption_usd) AS pending_redemption_usd,
       sum(s.earned_from_mcps_usd) AS from_mcps_usd,
       sum(s.earned_from_agents_usd) AS from_agents_usd,
       sum(s.earned_from_apps_usd) AS from_apps_usd,
       sum(s.earned_from_affiliates_usd) AS from_affiliates_usd,
       sum(s.earned_from_revenue_shares_usd) AS from_revenue_shares_usd
FROM creator_earnings_retirement_statements s
LEFT JOIN organizations o ON o.id = s.organization_id
WHERE s.status = 'frozen'
GROUP BY s.organization_id, o.name
ORDER BY unpaid_usd DESC;

-- In-flight redemptions an operator must reconcile or reject (no cron pays them now)
SELECT id, user_id, status, usd_value, network, broadcast_tx_hash, created_at
FROM token_redemptions
WHERE status IN ('pending', 'approved', 'processing')
ORDER BY created_at;

-- Mark one balance settled after paying it out of band
UPDATE creator_earnings_retirement_statements
SET status = 'settled_manually', settled_at = now(), settlement_reference = '<ticket or transfer id>'
WHERE user_id = '<user id>' AND status = 'frozen';
```

```sql
-- Affiliate earnings payable through Stripe Connect now, per user
WITH cutoff AS (
  SELECT e.user_id,
         COALESCE(s.frozen_at, (SELECT retired_at FROM creator_monetization_retirement)) AS since,
         CASE WHEN s.status = 'frozen' THEN s.available_balance_usd ELSE 0 END AS frozen_available,
         e.available_balance
  FROM redeemable_earnings e
  LEFT JOIN creator_earnings_retirement_statements s ON s.user_id = e.user_id
)
SELECT c.user_id,
       GREATEST(0, LEAST(COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), c.available_balance - c.frozen_available)) AS payable_usd
FROM cutoff c
LEFT JOIN redeemable_earnings_ledger l
  ON l.user_id = c.user_id AND l.earnings_source = 'affiliate'
 AND l.entry_type IN ('earning', 'adjustment') AND l.created_at > c.since
GROUP BY c.user_id, c.available_balance, c.frozen_available
HAVING GREATEST(0, LEAST(COALESCE(SUM(l.amount), 0), c.available_balance - c.frozen_available)) > 0;
```

### Paid MCP listings retired

With creator monetization retired, a listing price would bill buyers for revenue that reaches no creator.
- **Existing listings.** Migration **0502** makes every listing free: `pricing_type = 'free'`, both prices set to 0, x402 off. The prior pricing is saved in `metadata.retired_paid_listing` for audit. Usage history is untouched, and the column defaults are now free.
- **New prices refused.** `POST /api/v1/mcps` and `PUT /api/v1/mcps/:id` refuse any price with 410 `creator_monetization_retired` (capability `paid_mcp_listing`). Setting a listing to free is still allowed.
- **Proxy.** It never charges a listing price, even for a stale row. A free call skips the credit reservation, since zero-cost reservations are rejected. It runs the deferred strong credential check before calling upstream, then records usage at zero.
- **Editor.** The MCP editor no longer shows pricing or x402 controls. It explains that listings are free and always submits `pricingType: "free"`.
- **Not unlisted.** No listing was unlisted, because none has pricing that is intrinsic to the listing. x402 listings are made free too.

Listings affected by 0502. There is no local database, so run this before applying 0502, or use the `metadata` check after it:

```sql
-- Before 0502
SELECT id, organization_id, slug, name, status, is_public, pricing_type,
       credits_per_request, x402_price_usd, x402_enabled, total_requests
FROM user_mcps
WHERE pricing_type <> 'free' OR COALESCE(credits_per_request, 0) <> 0
   OR COALESCE(x402_price_usd, 0) <> 0 OR x402_enabled = true
ORDER BY total_requests DESC;

-- After 0502
SELECT id, organization_id, slug, name, status, metadata -> 'retired_paid_listing' AS previous_pricing
FROM user_mcps
WHERE metadata ? 'retired_paid_listing';
```

## #23020: affiliate surcharge disclosure

Fixes #23020

- **One formula.** `auto-top-up-charge-breakdown.ts` holds the formula shared by the durable charge snapshot and a new server preview. The formula, percentages, rounding and activation gate are unchanged.
- **Billing API.** `GET`/`PUT /api/v1/billing/settings` return `autoTopUp.chargePreview`: the credited base, affiliate markup, platform fee, total card charge, and whether attribution is `none`, `affiliate` or `unavailable`. `?previewAmount=` quotes an amount that has not been saved yet.
- **Billing UI.** The auto top-up card shows those lines as separate rows before the customer saves, and re-quotes on the server when the amount is edited. It never computes money in the client. When attribution is unavailable, it says no surcharge will be charged.
- **Receipts.** Invoices store `charge_breakdown`, parsed from the signed durable metadata. `GET /api/invoices/:id` and the ledger entries (`chargeBreakdown`) expose it, and the invoice page shows the markup, platform fee and total on separate lines. A breakdown whose lines do not add up to the charged total is never shown.
- **Other paths.** One-time checkout applies no affiliate surcharge, so it has nothing to disclose. MCP calls already recorded `base_amount_usd`, `affiliate_fee_usd` and `platform_fee_usd` on their credit transactions and usage rows.
- **Copy.** New UI copy is in `en.json`. The affiliate pricing example no longer promises a "redeemable token balance".

## #22967: frozen/sleeping retention

Fixes #22967

This builds on existing machinery rather than adding a parallel path: the billing-stop authority, the automatic resume from #30702, the Dedicated fallback `retain_until` from #32856, the sleep lifecycle, the email service and the backup `billing-freeze` retention reason, which previously had no writers.

- **Clock table.** 0501 adds `agent_funding_retentions`, one open row per stopped agent.
- **Hourly cron.** `/api/cron/agent-funding-retention` does the following:
  - **Discovery.** It finds provider-confirmed `billing_request` stops that are still the agent's latest decision (credits exhausted), and open plan-withdrawal fallbacks (plan lapsed past grace). The deadline is the stop time + 30 days, or the fallback's `retain_until`.
  - **Notices.** It sends the 7-day and 1-day deletion emails through the email service, using a new template with all 8 locales. Each notice is claimed on its row before sending and released if the send fails, so it goes out once and failures retry.
  - **No deletion without notice.**
    - A clock first seen late, such as an agent already stopped when this ships, gets a deadline at least 7 days out.
    - A deadline reached without the 1-day notice sends that notice and moves the deadline one day later.
  - **Deadline.** It enqueues the existing `agent_sleep` job, which proves a durable backup before removing the container. When the agent is `sleeping`, the latest backup is pinned for 90 days: v2 rows get `retention_reason = 'billing-freeze'` and `retention_until = now + 90d`. Legacy inline rows have no time-based GC.
  - **Paying resumes.** The existing resume paths restart the same agent id. The clock closes (`funding_restored`) once the agent is running or the fallback moved to recovery. It never deletes while an `agent_resume` or `agent_wake` job is in flight.
  - **Blocked case.** An agent stopped with an unbacked in-place runtime (#30746) is reported as blocked instead of losing state.

A $5 payout succeeds and a same-key retry deduplicates. A $3 payout that would reach the frozen balance is refused, and the remaining $2 succeeds. The frozen $15 is still intact;

## #31018 / #31328: dstack TEE deployment
Refs #31018, Refs #31328

This adds `packages/app/deploy/dstack-alpha/`, next to `Dockerfile.ci`, `confidential-bootstrap.mjs` and the existing sign, encrypt and provision tools it reuses.

- **Pinned image build.** `build-image.sh` builds `Dockerfile.ci` from digest-pinned node and bun bases listed in `image.lock.json`. `Dockerfile.ci` gains `NODE_IMAGE`/`BUN_IMAGE` args whose defaults are unchanged, and `verify-agent-image.sh` gains `DOCKER_BUILD_EXTRA_ARGS`. The script then overlays the digest-pinned `dstack-verifier` 0.6.0, pushes the image and records its registry digest.
- **Measured app-compose.** `scripts/alpha-dstack.ts render` writes the exact app-compose bytes. The compose pins the image by digest, keeps state on an `eliza-state` volume at `/data/eliza`, uses `restart: unless-stopped` and health-checks `/api/health`.
- **Model and ingress settings.** Text goes to Cerebras. Embeddings use Eliza Cloud or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and STT/TTS use Eliza Cloud. Local inference is off (plugin skipped, cloud deployment runtime, no local embeddings, no FFI llama). Ingress binds 0.0.0.0 and requires `ELIZA_API_TOKEN` (`ELIZA_REQUIRE_LOCAL_AUTH=1`). The `dstack-cpu` boot gate is on.
- **Secrets.** Secrets appear only as `allowed_envs` names. `encrypt-env` sends them through dstack's KMS-encrypted environment, and `confidential-bootstrap.mjs` authenticates them before the agent loads. No secrets are in the repo.
- **Attestation.** There is a new authenticated route, `POST /api/tee/dstack/attestation`, that returns raw guest evidence for an operator nonce. `verify-attestation` appraises it off-box with `verifyDstackAttestation` against the signed release. It also checks the signed Cerebras processor approval with `createConfidentialHostPolicy`.
- **README.** Covers deploy, verify, pairing, and upgrade/rollback.

Verification:

Refs #31021

- **core.** Adds a `remote-agent-pairing` contract (endpoints, bearer auth) and a strict QR/deep-link payload: `elizaos://remote/agent-pair?v=1&url=&code=&instance=`. The payload carries a one-time code and the issuing instance, never a token. The pair schemas gain an optional `instanceId`.

Before this change, pairing against a hosted agent-only server failed with `PAIRING_NOT_READY`. `pair-code` can now be read from loopback or with the API token, so a CVM operator can use it. `pair` rejects a code issued by another instance with 409.
- **app.** The compat `pair-code` route also admits an authenticated OWNER. The deep-link handler exchanges the code against a trusted origin (the build-pinned `VITE_ELIZA_REMOTE_FALLBACK_API_BASE` for Alpha APKs) before the normal connect, which asks the user to confirm.
- **ui.** `exchangeRemoteAgentPairing` checks the origin before sending any request and binds the exchange to the issuing instance.

topPRs.title: feat(cloud-billing): subscriptions + pay-as-you-go pricing policy (#22957 children)
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
Refs #22957

Eliza Cloud has two ways to pay: **Plus/Pro subscriptions** (a monthly allowance plus plan limits, from #32838/#32854) and **pay-as-you-go prepaid credits**. This PR puts the owner's decisions on the consolidated #22957 children into code, one commit per child. `packages/cloud` has no billing README, so the policy table is here.

| Policy | Decision (as implemented) |
|---|---|
| Storage prices (#22956) | `STORAGE_PRICING` in `shared/src/lib/constants/pricing.ts` is the only storage price source. PUT costs $0.0001 plus $0.000000001 per byte; GET, HEAD, list and presign cost $0.00005 each; DELETE is free. There is no per-GB fee. The `service_pricing` storage rows are a read-only copy, and the admin API refuses to edit them. |
| Top-ups and packs (#22963) | Pay-as-you-go top-ups accept any whole-cent amount from **$5 to $1,000** per checkout, on card, crypto and direct wallet. The $10/$25/$50/$100 buttons are presets, not packs. Credits always equal the amount paid, with no bonus. Fixed packs are retired, but historical pack orders and ledger rows can still be read. |
| API keys (#22958) | API keys are free. Plans cap how many a user can create: **pay-as-you-go 5, Plus 10, Pro 25**. Keys the system creates (default, explorer, sign-in, app and agent keys) don't count. A deactivated key counts until it is deleted. A key's own `rate_limit` (requests per minute across all endpoints) is a cap under the plan tier; it never raises the tier. |
| RPM tiers (#23019) | Subscribers get their plan's tier. For pay-as-you-go, the $5 and $100 thresholds count only **purchased** credits: Stripe, OxaPay crypto, x402, direct wallet (paid USD only, not the promo bonus) and payment requests. Refunds and chargebacks subtract; a won dispute adds back. Promo, signup, referral, affiliate, earnings, MCP and refund credits never count. |
| Crypto and x402 refunds (#22968) | Refunds are paid **only as Eliza Cloud credits**. Nothing is sent back on-chain or to fiat. Each refund is capped at the USD actually paid, can be replayed safely with the same refund key, and goes only to the org that owns the payment. The policy is stated at checkout and in the x402 top-up payment prompt. |
| Generated media (#20956) | Generated media counts toward the **single storage quota**; there is no separate media quota. If the quota is already full, the request is refused before any charge. If the output doesn't fit once generated, it isn't stored and the provider cost is charged. Storage is released only after the object is confirmed deleted. |

Migrations 0503–0505 are appended to the journal after develop's 0500–0502. They were first written as 0496–0498 and renumbered when #32907 merged, because the deployed migration ledger rejects entries inserted before already-applied migrations.

## #22956: storage pricing
Fixes #22956

- Every storage route now charges from `storageOperationPriceUsd`: objects PUT/GET/HEAD/DELETE, list and presign. None of them reads `service_pricing` any more, so the "pricing unavailable" 503 path is gone.
- Migration **0503** updates the storage rows in `service_pricing` to match the catalogue. It writes an audit row for any price it corrects and removes the old "finalize during pricing review" TODO.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/service-pricing` now returns 409 `storage_pricing_code_owned` for `service_id=storage`.
- Tests:
  - `storage-pricing-boundary.test.ts` pins the exact catalogue and proves no route reads DB pricing.
  - `storage-pricing-catalogue-migration.test.ts` applies 0503 on PGlite.

## #22963: credit packs and minimum top-up
Fixes #22963

- **Server:** `ORGANIZATION_CREDIT_CHECKOUT_LIMITS` is now $5–$1,000, and `ORGANIZATION_CREDIT_TOP_UP_PRESETS_USD` is [10, 25, 50, 100]. These bounds are read by:
  - card checkout (`/api/stripe/create-checkout-session`) and `/api/v1/credits/checkout`;
  - `/api/v1/credits/summary`;
  - crypto (`MIN/MAX_PAYMENT_AMOUNT`) and `/api/crypto/direct-payments`;
  - the billing-hold pay action.
- **Checkout orders:** `stripeCheckoutOrdersService.create` rejects new pack orders, amounts outside the range, and any grant that isn't exactly the charged amount (so no bonus). These are typed errors.
- **Removed:**
  - the pack checkout branch (a `creditPackId` now gets a typed 400);
  - `GET /api/stripe/credit-packs` (router regenerated);
  - the pack cache and service lookups;
  - the `seed-credit-packs` and `audit-credit-packs` scripts;
  - local-dev pack seeding;
  - `packSavingsPercent`.
- Migration **0504** deactivates the pack rows. Legacy pack settlement and quarantine are unchanged.
- **UI:** the billing tab has $10/$25/$50/$100 preset buttons and reads its limits from the contract. It previously had its own $1–$10,000 bounds.
- **Copy:** the billing SEO text in all eight locales (en, es, ja, ko, pt, tl, vi, zh-CN) now describes Plus/Pro subscriptions with a monthly allowance and pay-as-you-go top-ups from $5 to $1,000. No locale mentions credit packs any more.

## #22958: API keys
Fixes #22958

- `apiKeys` is now a resource ceiling:
  - added to `FREE_RESOURCE_CEILINGS` and to the Plus/Pro catalogue entries;
  - `readOrganizationQuotaPolicy` resolves it for pay-as-you-go and for subscriber orgs;
  - a lapsed subscription falls back to 5.
- `POST /api/v1/api-keys` creates through `createUserManaged`:
  - it takes the org policy lock and counts non-deleted user-created keys;
  - at the limit it throws `ApiKeyLimitExceededError`, returned as 403 `api_key_limit_exceeded` with `used`, `limit` and `remaining`;
  - rotating a key keeps its attribution.
- `GET` returns `usage`, and the API keys page shows it.
- Migration **0505** adds `api_keys.user_created`, backfills it for existing live user keys (system-provisioned keys are excluded), and adds a partial index.
- **Per-key `rate_limit`, now enforced.** Nothing read this field before, but keys do carry custom values: the explorer key is minted at 100, app keys at 10000, and the API accepts 1–100000. So the field is kept and enforced.
  - It means requests per minute for the key across every inference endpoint, and it only narrows the plan tier.
  - `enforceOrgRateLimit` takes the presenting `apiKeyId` and reads the cap inside the locked policy transaction. Policy admission now passes its transaction to the callback.
  - The cap is applied only when it can bind, i.e. when it is below the plan's combined per-minute tier. Default 1000 keys therefore add no work.
  - The admission Durable Object checks the tier window and the per-key window in one serialized decision. Key windows are dropped after their minute ends.
  - The Redis limiter path checks an `apikey:<id>:rpm` window.
  - A key that authenticated but has since disappeared fails closed with a 503.
  - Chat completions, chat, messages, embeddings and the generative routes pass the key id.
- Tests:
  - `api-key-plan-ceilings.pglite.test.ts`: the 5/10/25 ceilings, a refused 6th key, a deactivated key still counting, the slot freed on delete, org isolation, concurrent creates at N-1 admitting exactly one, and the Plus limit of 10.
  - `api-key-plan-ceilings-migration.test.ts`: the backfill.
  - `api-key-rate-limit.pglite.test.ts`: when a cap binds, and the fail-closed path for a missing or foreign key.
  - `inference-admission-gate.miniflare.test.ts`: the per-key window in the real Durable Object. It counts across endpoints, doesn't limit other keys or key-less callers, and rejects an invalid cap. 20 pass.

## #23019: RPM tier credit sources
Fixes #23019

- The metadata denylist is replaced by `ORG_TIER_PURCHASED_CREDIT_SOURCES`, an allowlist keyed on payment identity, and the total is net of reversals.
- Purchases, refunds and clawbacks now clear the cached tier, so a crypto or x402 purchase or a reversal takes effect without waiting out the one-hour cache.
- `org-rate-limit-purchased-credits.pglite.test.ts` covers every provenance, the $4.99/$5 and $99.99/$100 boundaries, clawback and reinstatement, org isolation and the Plus plan tier.

## #22968: crypto/x402 refunds
Fixes #22968

Fixes #20956

- The new `lib/storage/generated-media-storage.ts` is wired into image generation, `generate-music` and `generate-sfx`.
